entries.title: C0139: nontrivial percolation threshold under isoperimetric dimension greater than one
entries.statement: Historical open-problem target, current status unverified: for an infinite connected bounded-degree graph G satisfying |boundary_E S|>=c|S|^((d-1)/d) for every finite nonempty S, for some c>0 and d>1, must independent bond percolation have p_c(G)<1? The local intake attributes this to the Benjamini-Schramm conjecture in Pete lecture notes, Conjecture 12.7. Positive-Cheeger expansion is a stronger sufficient hypothesis; it does not cover the entire finite-dimensional isoperimetric condition. This goal card fills an exact C0139 anchor absent from the read-only population snapshot and supplies no claimed resolution.
assumptions: Uniform isoperimetric constant and dimension d>1

entries.title: Positive edge-Cheeger constant gives an explicit nontrivial bond threshold
entries.statement: Let G be an infinite connected graph of maximum degree D<infinity and edge-Cheeger constant h=inf_(finite nonempty S)|boundary_E S|/|S|>0. For independent bond percolation, 1/(D-1)<=p_c<=1/(1+h)<1. A simple-path first moment proves the lower bound. During cluster exploration after s discoveries and f failures, at least h(s+1)-f boundary edges remain untested. For p>1/(1+h), the comparison walk h+hs-f has positive drift and positive probability to remain positive forever, forcing an infinite cluster. This proves a positive-Cheeger special case; the drift argument does not decide critical equality or the full finite-dimensional isoperimetric conjecture.
entries.proof_text:
The cached Pete problem asks whether bounded-degree isoperimetric dimension >1 ensures p_c<1. The intake credits the dimension >4/Cayley results and leaves the non-Cayley intermediate regime unresolved. We give a self-contained stronger-hypothesis special case, not a new general resolution.

For an infinite connected graph of maximum degree D<infinity with edge-Cheeger constant h=inf_(finite nonempty S) |boundary_E S|/|S|>0, independent bond percolation satisfies

    1/(D-1) <= p_c <= 1/(1+h) < 1.

The lower bound is the union bound over at most D(D-1)^(r-1) simple paths of length r from a fixed vertex, for p(D-1)<1. To prove the upper bound, explore a cluster by testing only unrevealed edges from discovered vertices to undiscovered vertices. After s successful discoveries and f failures, the discovered set has s+1 vertices, and at least h(s+1)-f boundary edges remain untested. Thus the exploration cannot finish while Z=h+hs-f>0. The tests are an independent Bernoulli(p) sequence: each success adds h to Z and each failure subtracts 1. If p>1/(1+h), its drift is positive. For sufficiently small lambda>0, p exp(-lambda h)+(1-p) exp(lambda)<1. Then exp(-lambda Z), stopped at the first Z<=0, is a nonnegative supermartingale, and the probability ever reaching Z<=0 is at most exp(-lambda h)<1. With positive probability exploration never terminates, proving the upper bound. Critical equality itself is not decided by this drift argument. For the d-regular tree h=d-2, the upper bound matches its exact critical probability.

IP_(1+epsilon) does not supply a positive uniform h: the square lattice has a two-dimensional isoperimetric inequality but its square boxes have boundary/volume tending to zero. This explains the remaining gap rather than incorrectly applying the proved bound to the whole question.

entries.title: Finite isoperimetric dimension does not imply a positive Cheeger constant
entries.statement: Every finite nonempty S in the square lattice Z^2 has |boundary_E S|>=4sqrt(|S|), while the edge-Cheeger constant of Z^2 is zero. Indeed, if S occupies a columns and b rows then its edge boundary is at least 2a+2b>=4sqrt(ab)>=4sqrt(|S|); square boxes of side r have boundary/volume=4/r. Thus an IP_2 inequality cannot be substituted for the uniform positive-Cheeger hypothesis in the explicit threshold proof. This does not refute the conjecture that finite isoperimetric dimension greater than one ensures p_c<1.
